rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word da'f denotes animal hair and wool, used to make winter clothes.
rows.anchor: refers to the hair and wool of animals. They are used to produce winter clothes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding favours should make people recognize their noble, wise, merciful Creator, thank Him, and remember their obligation and accountability instead of worshipping others.
rows.anchor: each and everything of this universe is pointing to the fact that the creator of this universe is very noble and wise as well as merciful and compassionate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cattle are mentioned first because they were the Arabs' real wealth, supplying food, clothes, and many other benefits.
rows.anchor: cattle are mentioned the foremost because they were the real wealth of the Arabs. They obtained food, clothes and other multiple benefits from them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamāl means splendour, wealth, or grandeur, here represented by herds; a person's affluence and social status were judged by the size of his herds.
rows.anchor: here refers to splendour, wealth and grandeur and, as pointed out earlier, to their animal herds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although leaving for pasture would naturally precede returning, the verse reverses the order to foreground splendour, most visible in the evening when the herd is well-fed and fresh.
rows.anchor: the occasion of the discourse entails an expression of splendour and this is found more when the herd returns in the evening after grazing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels carried people and goods across long distances and hardships; in hot desert regions they were unrivalled, like God's ship.
rows.anchor: A camel can travel for very long distances and brave all kinds of hardships. In hot and desert areas specially, it was like the ship of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God affectionate and merciful teaches beneficiaries to recognize His rights, thank Him, worship Him alone, and avoid associating partners with Him; instead they become arrogant and thank others.
rows.anchor: His rights, thank Him and worship Him only. Moreover, they

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Horses, mules, and donkeys serve as transport and adornment when chiefs ride them; their mention reiterates that God grants these favours, yet people forget and worship others in pride.
rows.anchor: not only were used for transport by the Arabs but would also become a means of splendour when chiefs ride them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣd means straight; the construct phrase makes the straight path of monotheism a direct route to God, without side paths or intermediaries.
rows.anchor: The implication is that the straight path of monotheism makes a person reach God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deviant paths are human-made polytheistic routes that take people farther from God and make it difficult to return to monotheism.
rows.anchor: people have created deviant paths of polytheism in it. They tread upon them and then go further and further away from God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people choice and expects them to use reason and bear responsibility: monotheism reaches its destination, while deviation brings consequences; verse 37 likewise says God does not guide those led astray under His law.
rows.anchor: God has given the choice to people to adopt whatever they want to. He wants them to use their intellect and be responsible themselves for what they choose.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section II returns to monotheism through harmony among natural elements, warns that idols cannot help their worshippers, and says each person will face God, who knows and judges inner and outer selves.
rows.anchor: the topic of monotheism is once again taken up from another angle: harmony among conflicting elements of nature. People who rely on their deities are then warned that these make-belief idols will be not the slightest benefit them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asāmah means to drive animals toward their grazing grounds.
rows.anchor: The word أﺳﺎﻣﻪmeans to drive animals towards their grazing grounds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain and pasture benefiting animals show that one powerful, ever-living, wise God governs both heaven and earth and provides for animals.
rows.anchor: It is obvious that this harmony between the two clearly shows that the governance of a single wise being prevails in both these elements of nature.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse offers a proof of the hereafter: a world filled with wisdom and favours cannot be purposeless, so it must culminate in accountability.
rows.anchor: he instantly calls out that this world cannot be a purposeless place; God has not

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's purposeful wisdom and mercy imply a day when the responsible are rewarded and the indifferent held accountable.
rows.anchor: those who fulfilled their responsibilities are rewarded and those who led their lives indifferently are held accountable.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavenly bodies and day and night are placed in human service, yet people perversely worship these created favours and forget their Creator and the accountability they entail.
rows.anchor: instead of being grateful to God and keep in mind that these favours and privileges entail accountability, these naïve people have started to worship the very things that have been put to their service

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's variety was designed to reveal God's power, wisdom, mercy, and providence; every particle points to a Creator, if people pay attention and learn from what they see.
rows.anchor: every part of it is full of variety and diversity. Why? This is because its Creator wanted that wherever human beings look, they find some sign or the other of His power, wisdom, mercy and providence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection, understanding, and heed are listed in descending order: reflection is the highest faculty, leading from multiplicity to oneness and the universe's purpose; otherwise a person should at least reason and remember his destination.
rows.anchor: They are actually mentioned in a descending order.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere the sequence of hearing, understanding, and reflection ascends: at minimum a sane person should listen to sensible speech and try to understand it; one who cannot is like an animal on two legs.
rows.anchor: This, on the other hand, is an ascending order sequence.
